title: DSJR is Back, Here's What You Can Expect for Back-to-School Season
author: Dave Stuart Jr.
summary: In this short season-opener, Stuart announces a change to how he'll deliver back-to-school content: rather than trickling out twice-weekly newsletter articles over a month and a half, he's making the entire slate of back-to-school guides available immediately, while still drip-feeding them through the regular newsletter for subscribers who prefer that pace. He explains the scheduling problem behind the decision, schools nationally start anywhere from late July to after Labor Day, and previews that several of the new articles will be longer than his typical posts, in service of a stated goal to make his core ideas more accessible and actionable. The post closes as a table of contents for roughly twenty forthcoming guides distilling These 6 Things and The Will to Learn.
points: Stuart's rationale for releasing all back-to-school content at once is explicitly logistical: start dates vary by weeks across the country, so a fixed twice-weekly drip cannot serve everyone at the right moment.
He flags in advance that several forthcoming articles will run longer than usual, tying the choice to a prior goal of making his ideas more accessible and actionable.
The announcement doubles as an index, linking out to roughly twenty guides that distill the core nuggets of his two books, These 6 Things and The Will to Learn.
He frames the guides explicitly as companions to, not replacements for, the books, asking readers to keep buying them even as their ideas get online-ified.
quotes: The biggest problem I've had in the past with back-to-school season is that folks around the US and the world start school at different times, ranging roughly from late July to the week after Labor Day.
Well, I came up with a solution: this year, I'm making all of the blog articles for back-to-school season available right out of the gate. Starting today, you can click and go wherever you'd like.
This is in keeping with a goal I identified in my 23-24 year end reflection article: to make the core ideas I've written about over the past ten or so years more accessible and actionable.
So forgive me in advance for the longer articles. If you're ever tight for time, just ignore. I'll get back to briefer articles once these are out of the way.
My goal this school year is to help folks apprentice to the practices and ideas I've been writing about for years.
Please still buy them, even though I'm online-ifying many of their core ideas. It helps a lot.
